reason: The text portrays the Hebrews (Israelites) as an oppressed people suffering under Egyptian bondage (צַעֲקַת בְּנֵי־ יִשְׂרָאֵל בָּאָה אֵלַי - 'the cry of the children of Israel has come to me'; הַלַּחַץ - 'the oppression'), not as an active nation engaged in a political fight. The passage describes God hearing their cry and determining to deliver them through Moses, rather than depicting the Hebrews themselves fighting for political liberty. Furthermore, Egypt is explicitly the place of their captivity and suffering, not 'their own land.' The narrative focuses on divine intervention and deliverance, not Hebrew political or military resistance.
